title: Prove the consumer skill-override entry through Pi's real loader, in all four override states
statement: Prove, through the pinned Pi runtime's real resource loader, that the project-settings `skills` entry Kiln's settings merge produces - `../planning-content/skills-overrides`, written by `mergeSettingsText` and resolved relative to `.pi` - lets a consumer override of a generated stage skill win over the packaged skill of the same identity. Pi 0.84.4 resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources, and the first skill loaded with a given identity wins, so the consumer override wins over the packaged skill; it is not claimed to win over every earlier project-settings skill path. Cover the packaged-only, override-present, override-edited and override-skill-removed states for `kiln-stage-01-intake`, reading provenance from the loaded file path and Pi's collision diagnostic. This task writes no settings in production and adds no launch refusal: setup writes the entry (TSK-0060), and an absent override directory is measured as ignored, not refused.
notes: ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (F91, F94, D9). The statement said the override directory is registered after the packaged skills. Pi 0.84.4 does the reverse: its package manager ranks a project-settings entry ahead of a package resource before loading, and skill loading keeps the first skill with each name, so the override wins because it is resolved first. ⚠️ THIS TASK PROVES AN ENTRY; IT DOES NOT REGISTER ONE. The entry is already produced by CMP-0024's settings merge (`lib/pi-settings.mjs`), and writing it into a real project belongs to setup (TSK-0060). ⚠️ D9: AN ABSENT OVERRIDE DIRECTORY IS IGNORED. Pi skips a settings skill path that does not exist and reports nothing. This task records that behaviour as a control; a refusal for a missing directory, if one is ever wanted, belongs to setup or preflight, not to launch.
